extracted.intended_audience: C programmers writing PARI/GP library code or extensions (developers manipulating GEN objects and managing PARI stack/precision)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, assigning, copying, converting, and garbage-collecting PARI GEN objects from C, and for writing portable code across 32/64-bit architectures with correct precision handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symbolic precision/size macros for portability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided macros (BITS_IN_LONG, LONG_IS_64BIT, DEFAULTPREC, MEDDEFAULTPREC, BIGDEFAULTPREC) rather than hard-coded numeric values so programs run identically on 32-bit and 64-bit machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because prec sets the size of inexact results counted in (long) words (including codewords), the same numeric prec yields different bit accuracy on 32-bit vs 64-bit machines. Either use the DEFAULTPREC/MEDDEFAULTPREC/BIGDEFAULTPREC macros or conditional constructs like #ifndef LONG_IS_64BIT ... #else ... #endif (example: prec = MEDDEFAULTPREC). Note: half the accuracies available on 32-bit architectures (the odd ones) have no precise equivalents on 64-bit machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute bit and decimal accuracy from prec
rubrics_metrics.description: bit accuracy(prec) = (prec − 2) * BITS_IN_LONG; decimal accuracy = bit_accuracy * log(2)/log(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prec=5 ⇒ on 32-bit (BITS_IN_LONG=32) accuracy ≈ (5−2)*log(2^32)/log(10) ≈ 28 decimal digits; on 64-bit ≈ 57 digits. Use this when choosing prec to get desired numeric accuracy across architectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create PARI objects with cgetg(length,type)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN cgetg(long length, long type) creates a PARI object by allocating 'length' longwords and setting its type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: length must be correct: cgetg performs no checking, so giving an incorrect length causes disasters. Many types have predetermined lengths (e.g., 3 for t_INTMOD,t_FRAC,..., 4 for t_QUAD,t_QFI, 5 for t_PADIC,t_QFR). Prefer documented usage; most of the time you won't need cgetg because PARI functions return usable GENs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cgeti/cgetr for leaves (integers/reals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For creating leaves (integers or reals), use GEN cgeti(long length) and GEN cgetr(long length) instead of cgetg(..., t_INT/t_REAL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are very common and simpler. Macros lgetg, lgeti, lgetr are predefined synonyms for (long)cgetg, (long)cgeti, (long)cgetr respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: When constructing recursive/compound types, create all branches
rubrics_metrics.description: cgetg only creates the 'root' of recursive PARI types (e.g., matrices are row vectors of column vectors); you must create all sub-objects to build the full tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to create a 4×3 matrix, call z = cgetg(4, t_MAT); then for each column z[i] = lgetg(5, t_COL); then allocate each column's elements. Common mistake: assuming a single cgetg creates all nested structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand plain C assignment vs PARI assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: C assignment y = x moves the pointer; modifying x or y afterwards modifies the same underlying object. To copy PARI structure, use gaffect or gcopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical modification (e.g., x[1]=0) will change the other pointer. Use gaffect(GEN x, GEN y) to copy x into preexisting y (copies whole structure) or gcopy(GEN x) to create a new copy on the stack. Beware semantics and choose appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gaffect to assign PARI object structures with constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: void gaffect(GEN x, GEN y) copies structure of x into existing object y, but several conditions must be met for assignment to be possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed examples: assign integer into a real; forbidden: assign real into integer (use truncation/rounding functions instead). y must be large enough and have compatible tree structure (e.g., cannot assign non-zero integer into y if y has length 2). Changing precision of inexact objects is allowed; assignment of imprecise into a precise one usually 'does not make sense'. Functions ending in 'z' implicitly use gaffect (they record avma, perform op, gaf f ect result to last operand, restore avma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gaffsg to assign C long into PARI object
rubrics_metrics.description: void gaffsg(long s, GEN y) assigns an ordinary C long integer s into a PARI object y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for setting small integer values into PARI objects when appropriate. But generally avoid many gaf f ect statements unless for simple leaves or coercions (see exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer gerepile family to manual gaffect for garbage cleanup
rubrics_metrics.description: gerepile functions clean up stack garbage and update pointers safely; they are generally preferred over many manual gaffect usages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main function: GEN gerepile(long ltop, long lbot, GEN q) cleans stack between lbot and ltop, translates objects in [avma,lbot[ upward to abut ltop, updates pointers and returns updated q. Use idiom ltop=avma; ... lbot=avma; q=anything(); return gerepile(ltop,lbot,q). Beware of evaluation order pitfalls (e.g., gerepile(ltop, avma, anything()) is dangerous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep garbage connected for gerepile to work
rubrics_metrics.description: gerepile expects the garbage zone to be a connected interval; if garbage is interspersed with significant objects, gerepile may error or corrupt pointers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming idiom: arrange computations so garbage is contiguous between lbot and ltop. Example: compute p1 and p3 before p2 so p1 and p3 garbage become connected, then create container and use gerepile. If garbage cannot be made connected, use gerepilemany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gerepileupto when q is created before its components
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN gerepileupto(long ltop, GEN q) cleans stack between ltop and the connected object q and returns q updated; q must have been created before all its components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler to use in many cases because result is guaranteed to be suitable for gerepileupto if produced by documented PARI functions. But be careful to satisfy creation-order constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gerepilemany to preserve multiple results (robust)
rubrics_metrics.description: void gerepilemany(long ltop, GEN *gptr[], long n) cleans recent stack while updating n GEN pointers provided in array gptr; copies are done before cleaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need to preserve several objects (z1,z2,...) produced by computation; this is most robust but slower. To avoid copying when constraints hold, use gerepilemanysp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gerepilemanysp for faster but stricter updates
rubrics_metrics.description: void gerepilemanysp(long ltop, long lbot, GEN *gptr[], long n) cleans stack between lbot and ltop and updates GENs pointed by gptr without initial copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster but subject to same restrictions as gerepile (garbage connectivity, object adjacency). Less prone to user error is gerepilemany (with copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cgiv to give back the latest PARI object
rubrics_metrics.description: void cgiv(GEN z) destroys (gives back) the latest PARI object on the stack when saving avma is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when you want to free the very last object; cannot free objects not at the top of the stack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming idiom: record avma before creating garbage and restore after
rubrics_metrics.description: Record long ltop = avma before creating intermediate objects and later restore avma = ltop (or use gerepile) to discard garbage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example pattern: ltop=avma; garbage(); lbot=avma; q=anything(); return gerepile(ltop,lbot,q); Avoid returning gerepile(ltop, avma, anything()) due to compiler evaluation order unpredictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: For loops, use occasional gerepilemany when memory low
rubrics_metrics.description: In loops producing temporary objects, do garbage work each iteration but call gerepilemany only when memory (avma) crosses a threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: set limit = stack_lim(avma,1) instead of simple arithmetic to avoid overflow; when avma < limit, preserve needed objects (x,y,...) in a gptr array and call gerepilemany(ltop, gptr, n).

rubrics_metrics.name: When in doubt, force a copy then gerepileupto
rubrics_metrics.description: If stack is messy and you need a reliable way to keep results, use z = gerepileupto(ltop, gcopy(z)) to force a safe copy at bottom of stack, then clean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is slower but safe. For multiple results use gerepilemany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overuse of assignment statements; prefer gerepile for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Using gaffect and manual assignments is often inefficient and awkward; gerepile/gerepile* is usually preferred except in some small or controlled cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two exceptions where gaffect is acceptable: simple leaves whose size is controlled, and to coerce an inexact object to a given precision (example: gaffect(x, (tmp=cgetr(3))); x = tmp;). Using preallocated large objects with gaddz/gaddz-style in-place ops can avoid gerepile but is often slower and more cumbersome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory layout law for gerepile relocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a given PARI object is to be relocated by gerepile then, apart from universal objects, the chunks of memory used by its components should be in consecutive memory locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented PARI functions guarantee this. If objects become disconnected (garbage interspersed), gerepile may fail to update pointers correctly — be wary when allowing objects to become disconnected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of non-checking macros for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros handling codewords and type/length (typ, settyp, lg, setlg, signe, setsigne, lgef, setlgef, varn, setvarn, expo, setexpo, etc.) do not check types for efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use them correctly; they accept arguments without explicit casts and assume correct types. Misuse will produce incorrect behavior without safety checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-specific internal representation rules (integers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type t_INT second codeword z[1] contains sign (1,0,-1) and effective length (number of significant longwords), and integers are normalized so first mantissa longword z[2] is non-zero (except 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize zero by sign==0 or effective length==2. Absolute value is represented in base 2^BITS_IN_LONG by (z[2],z[3],...,z[lgefint(z)-1]). Use mpodd and mod2..mod64 macros for fast residue checks (they return long, avoid stack clutter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-specific internal representation rules (reals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type t_REAL second codeword z[1] encodes sign and a biased binary exponent (bias HIGHEXPOBIT). Mantissa is normalized: z[2] most significant bit is 1 when non-zero; mantissa words represent number between 1 (included) and 2 (excluded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not detect real zero by checking z[2] (it may be defined and 0); use sign==0. Use expo()/setexpo() to access unbiased exponent. Note dbltor(double s) yields about 19 decimal digits (but on 32-bit only ~16 significant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-specific rules for modular/polynomial/p-adic types
rubrics_metrics.description: Each composite type has structural constraints: t_INTMOD has z[1]=modulus, z[2]=class (both integers) with 0≤z[2]<z[1]; t_POLMOD analogous for polynomials; t_FRAC/t_FRACN have z[1]=numerator,z[2]=denominator (integers), and may be reduced with gred; t_PADIC encodes precision, biased exponent and components at z[2],z[3],z[4]; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep modulus objects on the heap to share them among objects instead of making stack copies. For p-adics use precp/valp accessors; a p-adic z ≠ 0 satisfies z = p^valp(z) * (z[4] + O(pprecp(z))). Follow chapter-specific hierarchy rules for polymods and variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomials and power series conventions and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Type t_POL second codeword contains sign, variable number, and effective length; coefficients are in ascending order z[2]..z[lgef(z)-1]; degree = effective_length - 3; zero polynomial may have eﬀective length > 2 if leading coefficient is not an exact zero. Type t_SER has sign, variable number and biased exponent (HIGHVALPBIT); do not use expo/setexpo on power series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lgef/gvar/degree to inspect polynomials. Be careful distinguishing exact zero coefficients from approximate zeros in series/polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy vs forcecopy vs clone semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN gcopy(GEN x) creates a new copy on the stack but does not duplicate universal components (it copies only pointers to them). GEN forcecopy(GEN x) forces a complete copy. GEN gclone(GEN x) creates a permanent heap copy; void gunclone(GEN x) deletes a clone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you copy a clone back to the stack and then delete it, use forcecopy not gcopy to avoid missing components (e.g., moduli). No PARI object should keep references to a clone after it has been destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions between C and PARI types
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided conversion functions: GEN stoi(long s), GEN dbltor(double s), long itos(GEN x), double rtodbl(GEN x), long gtolong(GEN x), double gtodouble(GEN x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of accuracy limits: dbltor yields about 19 decimal digits but on 32-bit only ~16 are significant. Use appropriate conversion routines for your needs.
